_rule: Hook = the first 1.5 seconds. Number in the first line, second person, present tense, no throat-clearing. The claim must have a citation waiting.
first_1_5s_rules: 1 · Number in the first line — a precise figure reads as evidence, not opinion
2 · Second person, present tense — 'you / your / right now' forces a self-scan
3 · No throat-clearing — first 3 words carry the whole claim
4 · Visual contradicts or amplifies the words — scale reference on screen
5 · One idea, one frame — two claims in 1.5s = zero claims
6 · The claim must have a citation waiting — payoff by second 5-8, never in the hook
7 · Motion or face by frame 3 — never a still logo
three_word_test: Write the first three words on their own line. No tension = dead hook.

reframe_hook_bank.hook: You don't have abs. You have a pressure canister.
You don't lift with muscles. You lift with permission.
Your lungs aren't bags. They're a ragged sheet folded into your chest.
reframe_hook_bank.note: surface-area figure must match the Numbers Registry

reframe_hook_bank.hook: You're not tired. Your battery is mid-recycle.
Fat isn't storage. It's an organ that talks.
Soreness isn't damage healing. It's an alarm that's miscalibrated.
You don't burn fat in the gym. You sign the invoice there and pay it in your sleep.
reframe_hook_bank.cite: EPOC literature — keep the <7% honesty bound

reframe_hook_bank.hook: Your bones aren't scaffolding. They're a bank that pays out calcium every day.
Thirst is a late alarm — feel it and you're already down about 2%.
Willpower isn't a muscle you're missing. It's a system you haven't built.
Your heart doesn't beat 'a lot'. It beats about 100,000 times today. No day off.
Your gut runs on about 500 million neurons — more than a cat's brain.
Metabolism isn't a speed. It's a thermostat that fights back.
You don't have one clock. You have about ten, all reading different times.
A muscle doesn't 'tone'. It grows or it shrinks. Tone is just fat leaving the room.

ready_hooks_20.hook: The gap your every thought jumps across is about 20 nanometres — thousands of times thinner than a hair.
Your motivation isn't a personality trait. It's a dopamine curve — and you can train its shape.
Your grip is measured in your brain before it's measured in your hand. Here's why beginners plateau.
You take about 12 breaths a minute and never think about the wall that makes it work — about 0.3 micrometres at its thinnest.
Spread your lungs flat and they'd cover half a tennis court. Now here's why you gas out in 30 seconds anyway.
You're not out of shape. Your breathing muscles are untrained — and that's a fixable number.
Right now, doing nothing, you're recycling roughly your bodyweight in fuels today — an estimate, and a staggering one.
The 'fat-burning zone' is real — and it isn't where the research says you should live. Here's the crossover point.
Your metabolism isn't slow. You're eating about 400 calories a day you can't see. Let me show you where.
You are about 42 litres of water in a 70-kilo frame — and your brain is roughly 73% of it.
ready_hooks_20.cite: Buono & Kolkhorst / Gray's, 70 kg reference body

ready_hooks_20.hook: Sweat is not fat crying. Here's what you're actually losing on that run.
Down 2% on water and your strength drops before you feel thirsty. That's why your last set failed.
You have 206 bones, and about 99% of your calcium is locked inside them — not floating in your blood.
The hardest thing in your body isn't bone. It's the enamel on your teeth. Here's what that teaches us about load.
You'll get a nearly-new skeleton about every 10 years — training decides what it's rebuilt from.
If you have PCOS, your body handles the same plate of rice differently. Your training should too — here's the number.
After 30 you lose roughly 1% of muscle a year — unless you do one thing. It isn't cardio.
Your strength isn't the same across the month. Here's how to train with your physiology — and where the evidence is still thin.
20 minutes done right beats 60 done wrong. Here's the heart-rate math nobody shows you.
You're made of five systems. You only train one. Find out which of yours is the weak link — free Body-Scan.

do_not_list: No woo words (see Forbidden Lexicon in docs/BRAND-GUARDRAILS.md)
No fear-bait (hooks must resolve honestly to the cited payoff)
No bait-and-switch (CTA must match the content)
No strawman myths — kill a real, popular belief
No correlation sold as causation (mortality hooks: say 'associated with', name the proxy)
No borrowed signature lines un-attributed (attribute or originate)
screenshot_proof_test: Freeze the hook frame. Could a rival trainer, a physio or a doctor screenshot it and mock it? If yes → rewrite the frame.
